title: 257. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Horizontal and Vertical Lines as Relations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the equation of a vertical line.
questions.question: Which equation represents a vertical line?
questions.explanation: A vertical line has an equation of the form \(x=a\), where \(a\) is a constant. The graph of \(x=3\) is the vertical line passing through \((3,0)\). The equation \(y=3\) represents a horizontal line. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: A vertical line fixes the \(x\)-value and allows all real \(y\)-values.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the equation of a horizontal line.
questions.question: Which equation represents a horizontal line?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line has an equation of the form \(y=b\), where \(b\) is a constant. The graph of \(y=-2\) is the horizontal line passing through \((0,-2)\). The equation \(x=-2\) represents a vertical line. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: A horizontal line fixes the \(y\)-value and allows all real \(x\)-values.

questions.concept: Vertical Line Test for a Vertical Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a vertical line represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\).
questions.question: Does the vertical line \(x=4\) represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because one \(x\)-value corresponds to infinitely many \(y\)-values.

questions.explanation: The graph of \(x=4\) contains all points of the form \((4,y)\) for every real number \(y\). Thus the input \(x=4\) corresponds to infinitely many outputs. A function must assign exactly one output to each input, so the vertical line does not represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether any vertical line intersects the graph more than once.

questions.concept: Vertical Line Test for a Horizontal Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a horizontal line represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\).
questions.question: Does the horizontal line \(y=5\) represent \(y\) as a function of \(x\)?

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because every \(x\)-value gives exactly one \(y\)-value.

questions.explanation: For every real number \(x\), the point \((x,5)\) lies on the horizontal line. Thus each input \(x\) corresponds to exactly one output \(y=5\). Therefore the horizontal line represents \(y\) as a function of \(x\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether each \(x\)-value produces exactly one \(y\)-value.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the slope of a vertical line.
questions.question: What is the slope of the vertical line \(x=-1\)?
questions.explanation: A vertical line has no defined slope because the change in \(x\) between any two points is zero, and slope is defined as the change in \(y\) divided by the change in \(x\). Division by zero is undefined. Therefore the slope of \(x=-1\) is undefined, so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Recall that slope is \(\frac{\text{change in }y}{\text{change in }x}\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify the slope of a horizontal line.
questions.question: What is the slope of the horizontal line \(y=7\)?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line has no vertical change between any two points. Its slope is \(\frac{0}{\text{change in }x}=0\). Therefore the slope of \(y=7\) is \(0\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: For a horizontal line, the change in \(y\) is zero.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a vertical line.
questions.question: What is the domain of the vertical line \(x=2\)?
questions.explanation: The vertical line \(x=2\) contains only points with \(x\)-coordinate \(2\). Therefore the only input value in the domain is \(2\). Hence the domain is \(\{2\}\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: List all \(x\)-values for which the graph has a point.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a horizontal line.
questions.question: What is the range of the horizontal line \(y=-3\)?
questions.explanation: The horizontal line \(y=-3\) contains only points with \(y\)-coordinate \(-3\). Therefore the only output value in the range is \(-3\). Hence the range is \(\{-3\}\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: List all \(y\)-values for which the graph has a point.

questions.concept: Identifying a Relation That Is Not a Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine which line does not represent a function of \(x\).
questions.question: Which relation is not a function of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(x=-6\) is a vertical line. For the input \(x=-6\), there are infinitely many \(y\)-values, so it is not a function. The graph of \(y=-6\) is a horizontal line, and each \(x\)-value gives exactly one \(y\)-value, so it is a function. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Apply the vertical line test to each relation.

questions.concept: Equation of a Horizontal Line Through a Point
questions.learningObjective: Determine the equation of a horizontal line passing through a given point.
questions.question: Which line passes through \((2,5)\) and is horizontal?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line has an equation of the form \(y=b\). Since the line passes through \((2,5)\), the \(y\)-coordinate is \(5\), so the equation is \(y=5\). The equation \(x=2\) represents a vertical line. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: A horizontal line has the same \(y\)-value for every point on it.
